title: Introduce compatibility bridge for phased deprecation coercion of tool envelopes
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: We are rolling out a breaking schema change to the tool/function-call envelope shape (tool->tool_call, args typed differently) that will improve structured output guarantees for downstream clients. Many customers and SDKs still rely on the legacy envelope shape, and we need a staged deprecation path that keeps streaming stable and minimizes sudden client breakage.

This PR introduces a runtime compatibility bridge that performs a staged, opt-in coercion and soft-fallback for deprecated tool envelopes. The bridge supports three modes: off (default), permissive-optin (beta header + header-backed telemetry), and strict (coercion + 422 enforcement). It also integrates with streaming path, ensuring the envelope rewrite is safe for chunked responses and preserves tool-call tokens and ordering.

What this change does (high level):
- runtime/openai_compat/compat_bridge: new middleware that inspects Accept-Compat and X-Redwood-Compat-Mode headers and applies in-line mapping from legacy tool envelopes to the new typed envelope. Mapping is intentionally conservative (string->json coercion attempted first; fallback to original payload if coercion fails and mode=permissive).
- streaming: adds careful buffer boundaries to the stream transform so we never split a JSON envelope across chunks during rewrite; adds unit and e2e tests that replay recorded chunked responses.
- telemetry: emits compat.mode, compat.coercions_attempted, compat.coercions_failed, and compat.fallback_used tags on request traces and a lightweight metric for early rollout monitoring.
- API/Docs: documents the beta header X-Redwood-Compat-Mode and the opt-in process; adds a migration guide and suggested client heuristics.
- CLI/installer: adds a toggle for private deployments to enable permissive rollout by default for internal-only clusters.

Backward compatibility guarantees: When mode is off we do nothing. When mode=permissive we attempt to coerce but fall back to original envelope if coercion fails; when mode=strict we coerce and return a structured error for unrecoverable envelopes. The bridge is idempotent (re-applying it is a no-op) and safe across retries.

Testing and rollout plan: start with permissive-optin via beta header for a subset of internal customers and SDKs. Monitor compat.coercions_failed < 0.5% and compat.fallback_used trends for 48h before expanding. Strict mode will be gated behind a feature flag and a communication window (60 days) after permissive opt-in is stable.

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-1421, PM-87, SUP-310.

Notes: This is intentionally conservative — it avoids any automatic rewrite in the hosted default path, and logs deprecation notices through response headers and the console. The PR includes unit tests, integration tests against the streaming harness, and a small compatibility regression job for SDKs.

3 commits:
- a1b2c3d: runtime: add compat_bridge middleware and envelope mappers
- 4d5e6f7: streaming: add chunk-preserving transform + tests
- 8f9a0b1: docs/cli: add migration guide and private-installer toggle
release_notes: Adds an opt-in compatibility bridge for legacy tool envelopes. No default behavioral changes for hosted customers. Introduces X-Redwood-Compat-Mode header (permissive|strict) to opt into coercion behavior; emits telemetry for rollout monitoring.
review_comments:
Ethan: Can we make the mapping logic configurable per-customer so enterprise tenants with custom tool schemas can add rules?
Priya: Added a plug-in hook and documented how to register a mapping rule for dedicated/private in runtime/openai_compat/README.md. Kept default behavior unchanged.
María: Streaming transform looks good, but add an end-to-end test that simulates a client abort mid-stream.
Priya: Added test (streaming/tests/test_client_abort_rewrites.py) and a guard that rolls back partial rewrites on client abort.
Samir: Request to add a metric for compat.latency_p95 with and without coercion.
Priya: Added compat.latency_p95 and included it in the perf dashboard snapshot for the rollout canary.
ci_log_summary: Initial CI: fail (flake in streaming harness). Reran focused tests; streaming harness flake fixed by adding a deterministic replay seed. Full CI passed on rerun.
integration_checks: Included integration replays against recorded chunked responses; SDK compatibility tests exercised beta header. No SDK-breaking failures observed in staging.
notes_for_ops: When enabling permissive rollout in production, watch compat.coercions_failed, compat.fallback_used, and compat.latency_p95. Alert if coercions_failed > 1% sustained for 30m. Provide ops playbook steps in docs/api/migration/tool-envelope-deprecation.md.
changelog_entry: Opt-in compatibility bridge for legacy tool envelopes: beta header X-Redwood-Compat-Mode added; permissive coercion path available for staged migration. See migration guide.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Schedule 2-week canary and metric review. 2) Notify SDK leads to opt into beta. 3) Prepare deprecation announcement when strict toggle is enabled.
misc: The runtime mapping intentionally avoids deep type coercions (no automatic schema inference). For complex cases, customers should provide explicit mapping rules via the plugin hook; examples are in the README.
